Thought I'd share my results as the season winds down. Have not gardened in years and it showed.

Got my raised beds done beginning of May. Quite small but each suitable for a few plants.

Put in amended soil in each (clean fill, vegetable matter compost, manure, & peat).

Planted seeds butternut squash, peppers, cukes, bush beans, and some sunchokes I forgot about in the bottom of the vegetable drawer.

Same soil used for potted herbs from growing plants, thyme, basil, peppermint, rosemary, & sage, seeds for more basil, + dill & cilantro.

Rows of radishes planted near herbs in front of house.

Watering diligent, and plenty of sun in all spots.

FAIL: Butternut squash has done nothing but produce male flowers on 3 vines all year. Flowers bloom & drop off, none become squash.

FAIL: Peppers grew ~4" (four inches) and have stayed that height all season. They just sit there in stasis.

FAIL: Bush beans grew to ~1-foot, no flowers just leaves.

FAIL: Basil sprouted & stayed at ~1-inch then deer or chipmunks ate them as well as store bought plant that was doing great.

FAIL: Dill sprouted grew to ~2" & died.

FAIL: Cilantro never germinated.

FAIL: Radish greens eaten by chipmunks or deer, entire thriving set of rows stripped.

PARTIAL FAIL: Rosemary eaten once by deer or chipmunks, moved inside to recover.

NEUTRAL: Peppermint grew bigger than when purchased, does not look robust or full in pot.

NEUTRAL: Thyme grew bigger than when purchased, does not look robust or full in pot.

PARTIAL SUCCESS: Planted 6 cuke spots, only 2 germinated & grew and those produce. Lots of 2.5" x 10" sweet cukes from them.

SUCCESS: Sage robust, plant 3-4x size from when purchased.

SUCCESS: Sunchokes all sprouted, plants 4-5 feet tall. No flowers, should do that next year. Planted in crappy clay soil, they don't care.

IMO my soil mix was bad for some plants (peppers) but fine for cukes planted in same raised bed. The butternut squash a mystery as continual male flower production not normal. Have to be more proactive on pest control, did not know deer even went into my front yard as not easy access if they were the culprits. Chipmunks always a problem but did not think they'd go for the radishes (or other greens). Have grown them before without issue. Seeds not germinating at all a mystery, all seed were fresh purchases this year.

Not sure yet what my all takeaways are and will appreciate comments.
This season, some hits & mostly misses...

How does your soil drain? It sounds like some plants could have either been over-watered or having trouble with the density of the soil. My soil has a LOT of clay, which has its benefits but one downside is that it will either not get enough water and is super hard for the plants to push through, or get waterlogged and not drain. This was my first thought.

I don't know how the plants you mentioned respond to over-fertilization, but it doesn't sound like you're low on firts, and this could cause problems. Are you noticing any burning on the edges of the leaves? Are the pepper plants leaves soft and dark green, or robust and medium/light green?

I know it shouldn't matter much, but you might want to take a sample of the soil you used, and test the PH of the water before and after it drains through your soil. Rain water doesn't matter, but if the PH of your house water is off, it could mean inhibiting the uptake of nutrients through the roots. Different plants have different ranges that are ideal. You may have some imbalances there that are causing problems for some plants but not others. It's possible some of your amendments are throwing the balance of the soil off for some plants.

Also one HUGE thing to mention is: This is your first season (On that soil). If you cover your beds with straw, wood-chips, or at the very least cardboard to overwinter, I think you'll find that your second season in this location might be more fruitful. I'm a big proponent of the permaculture/food forest techniques, and letting the insects in the soil naturally amend the earth takes time but is worth it.

That's just my 1000 foot view, though. I'm going through the checklist that I found works for troubleshooting, and it's possible there's something totally different causing the problems, like your specific area, the vendor of the seeds, etc.

Drainage great on beds but a couple of the pots (ones that did not produce well) poor. Soil looks almost silty. I plan to repot those for overwintering inside.

None of any plants have burned edges although some of the butternut squash leaves have turned yellow and dropped off as long as they've been growing. Pepper plants have the right color, med/light green but suspended growing. This one is just weird.

Regarding amended soil & PH, I am leaning towards something just being off and as you said, affects some plants and not others. Have grown in this spot before with VG results. Have not grown with this soil however. Going to clean it all out for next year or condition it as you suggest for next.

Appreciate your feedback very much. Not discouraged by my results, the data will be useful especially on the pest marauding.
